Double machine learning for panels with fixed effects

Source: R/panel_causal.R
plndml.Rd

The effect of a treatment (continuous or binary) on an outcome in a unit-by-period panel, with unit and period fixed effects removed and the confounding through covariates fitted by a machine learner, cross-fitted by unit, with an orthogonal (Neyman) score and errors clustered by unit.

Usage

plndml(
  data,
  unit,
  time,
  y,
  trt,
  covs,
  fe = c("unit", "time"),
  lrn = "lasso",
  basis = c("linear", "poly2"),
  folds = 5L,
  nrep = 1L,
  seed = 1L,
  cl = NULL,
  conflvl = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

trt

Column name of the treatment (continuous, or 0/1).

covs

Column names of the time-varying covariates.

fe

c("unit", "time") (default) or "time".

lrn

"lasso" (default), "ridge", "ols", or a function.

basis

"linear" (default) or "poly2".

folds

Cross-fitting folds of units (default 5).

nrep

Repeated sample splits (default 1).

seed

Seed for the folds (default 1).

cl

Column name of the clusters (default the unit), or two column names for two-way clustering (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2011): \(V_a + V_b - V_{ab}\), each term with the small-sample factor of the dimension with fewer clusters, and t on its \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom. A composite cluster (district by month, say) is one column made with interaction().

conflvl

Confidence level (default 0.95).

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_dml: estimate, se, lower, upper, t, p_value; attributes n, clusters, learner, folds, repeats, and r2 (the out-of-fold R-squared of the two nuisance fits).

Details

The model is the partially linear panel model $$Y_{it} = \theta D_{it} + g(X_{it}) + \alpha_i + \gamma_t + \varepsilon_{it}.$$ Following Clarke and Polselli (2025), the fixed effects are removed by the within transformation (\(\tilde Y\), \(\tilde D\), \(\tilde X\)), and \(\ell(\tilde X) = E(\tilde Y \mid \tilde X)\) and \(m(\tilde X) = E(\tilde D \mid \tilde X)\) are fitted by the learner on \(K\) folds of units (all of a unit's periods in one fold, so a unit's own errors never help predict it). With the out-of-fold residuals \(U = \tilde Y - \hat\ell\) and \(V = \tilde D - \hat m\), the partialling-out estimator is $$\hat\theta = \sum V U / \sum V^2,$$ the solution of the Neyman-orthogonal score \((U - \theta V) V\) of Chernozhukov et al. (2018). Its variance is the cluster-robust sandwich over units, $$\hat V = \frac{G}{G - 1} \frac{\sum_g \big(\sum_{i \in g} V_i (U_i - \hat\theta V_i)\big)^2}{(\sum V^2)^2},$$ with t on \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom. Folds are drawn with seed; nrep repeated splits are combined by the median of the estimates and of the variances plus the squared deviations from it (Chernozhukov et al. 2018, section 3.4).

Learners, all in base R: "lasso" (coordinate descent, penalty by 5-fold cross-validation), "ridge" (penalty by generalised cross-validation), "ols", or a function returning predictions (for example a random forest from another package), called as function(x_train, y_train, x_test). basis = "poly2" adds squares and pairwise products of the covariates, built from the covariates as observed and then demeaned, so a confounding that is a combination of them is removed exactly. The demeaned features are what the learners see: a covariate fixed within a unit is absorbed by the unit effect and carries no information. A learner given only the demeaned covariates (a random forest, say) approximates a nonlinear confounding less well; the poly2 basis, or a basis of the user's own as further covariates, is the remedy.

References

Chernozhukov V, Chetverikov D, Demirer M, Duflo E, Hansen C, Newey W, Robins J (2018). Double/debiased machine learning for treatment and structural parameters. The Econometrics Journal 21(1):C1-C68. doi:10.1111/ectj.12097

Clarke PS, Polselli A (2025). Double machine learning for static panel models with fixed effects. The Econometrics Journal 29:69-86. doi:10.1093/ectj/utaf011

See also

plrcf (one cross-section), stgatt with covariates (doubly robust difference in differences).

Examples

p <- polex()
set.seed(9)
p$unemployment <- 6 + sin(p$month / 6) + stats::rnorm(nrow(p), 0, 0.5)
p$patrols <- 0.5 * p$unemployment + p$reformed + stats::rnorm(nrow(p))
plndml(p, "district", "month", "crmrate", "patrols",
          c("unemployment", "arrrate"), lrn = "ridge")
#> Double machine learning with fixed effects (ridge, 5 folds of units, 1 split)
#>  estimate      se   lower   upper      t   p_value
#>   -0.2957 0.05072 -0.4019 -0.1896 -5.831 1.287e-05
#> 720 observations, 20 clusters; out-of-fold R-squared: outcome -0.000, treatment 0.081
